fonts.serifDisplay: Playfair Display, Cormorant Garamond, or similar high-contrast serif
fonts.monoPanel: IBM Plex Mono, JetBrains Mono, or similar
fonts.body: Inter, Work Sans, or a clean legible geometric/humanist sans

scale.h1: text-5xl sm:text-6xl md:text-7xl font-serif-display tracking-tight leading-none text-stone-900
scale.eyebrow: text-xs md:text-sm font-mono-panel tracking-[0.2em] uppercase text-stone-500

visual_enhancers.texture: Include a class `paper-grain` applied globally using a very subtle CSS radial-gradient noise or SVG texture overlay (opacity 2-4%, mix-blend-mode: multiply).
visual_enhancers.borders: 1px solid borders using stone-200 or stone-300. Sharp edges (rounded-sm or rounded-none) to evoke print/paper.
visual_enhancers.shadows: Minimal to zero shadows. Rely on border and background color contrast. No soft/large shadows.

Screen1_Landing.structure: Editorial grid, heavily relying on negative space. Mobile-first stacking.

sections.name: Header
sections.composition: Minimalist. Logo (Serif) on left, 'Open Compass' (secondary action, subtle stone-600 hover:stone-900) on right.
sections.alignment: flex justify-between items-center py-6 px-8 md:px-12 border-b border-stone-200

sections.name: Hero Story
sections.composition: Massive left padding or off-center alignment (e.g., col-span-8 in a 12-col grid). Avoid centered text. Large spacing (py-32).

elements.content: Writing is thinking. Don't let a machine do it for them.
elements.style: font-serif-display text-5xl md:text-7xl text-stone-900 max-w-4xl mb-8

elements.content: Most tools write for your students. Compass asks the right questions, forcing them to construct understanding themselves. It's not a co-author. It's a developmental studio.

sections.name: Primary Action Area
sections.composition: A distinct interactive zone positioned as a natural next step below the subcopy.

elements.style: bg-[#8C3A2A] text-white px-8 py-4 rounded-sm font-medium hover:bg-[#6B2C20] transition-colors inline-block

elements.content: A 3-minute, in-character experience. No signup required.

Screen2_Bridge.psychological_question: Could I use this with my own students?
Screen2_Bridge.structure: A narrow, focused column centered in the viewport. It should feel like a quiet room after a profound realization.

sections.name: Reflection Zone
sections.composition: Centered layout (the only centered part of the app) to create a 'pause' moment. Padded heavily (py-32).

elements.content: Notice what just happened. You didn't read a guide, and the machine didn't write it for you. You were led to the insight. Imagine your students experiencing that exact shift in perspective.

sections.name: Action Zone
sections.composition: Flex column or row, centered. Clear primary vs secondary hierarchy.

elements.style: bg-[#8C3A2A] text-white px-6 py-3 rounded-sm font-medium hover:bg-[#6B2C20] transition-colors mb-4 md:mb-0 md:mr-4
text-stone-500 hover:text-stone-900 underline underline-offset-4 decoration-stone-300 transition-colors px-6 py-3

motion.philosophy: Restrained, organic, breathing. No bouncy spring animations. Everything feels like ink settling into paper.
motion.page_load: Framer Motion: initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 10 }} animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }} transition={{ duration: 0.8, ease: [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1] }}
motion.button_hover: Framer Motion: whileHover={{ scale: 1.02 }} transition={{ duration: 0.2 }}

accessibility.contrast: Strict adherence to WCAG AA. Ensure #8C3A2A on #faf9f6 passes.
accessibility.focus: Focus rings should be sharp, using stone-400 or the accent #8C3A2A. e.g., focus:ring-2 focus:ring-[#8C3A2A] focus:outline-none.
accessibility.aria: Use proper aria-labels on links and buttons.

media.strategy: No photography. The 'studio' aesthetic relies purely on typography, spatial rhythm, and the paper grain texture. Empty space IS the primary visual asset.

instructions_to_main_agent: Implement the `paper-grain` class using a subtle SVG noise background or CSS radial-gradient. Apply it to the body or main wrapper.
Configure custom colors in Tailwind config: `brand: { paper: '#faf9f6', accent: '#8C3A2A', accentHover: '#6B2C20' }`.
Avoid Shadcn/UI for these specific pages if it forces a generic 'card' look. Build raw Tailwind divs for the editorial, sharp-edged flat look.
Ensure all buttons and links have `data-testid` attributes (e.g., `data-testid='landing-try-preview'`).
DO NOT use a transparent background for the nav header. Give it the paper color `#faf9f6` or a very subtle border/opacity to separate from content.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Do not use dark colors as gradients.
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling. Use asymmetrical or editorial alignments.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Subtle grain textures, custom cursors, and restrained motion separate good from extraordinary.
All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a `data-testid` attribute.
For this specific 'Compass' project, avoid glassmorphism, bright neons, or SaaS purple. Stick to the literary, paper-like studio aesthetic requested.
